html:
Muhammad was the Arab prophet and leader who founded Islam, born in Mecca in western Arabia around 570 and died in Medina in 632. Muslims believe he was the last prophet sent by God, after Abraham, Moses and Jesus.

He was orphaned young and raised by his grandfather and his uncle. He worked as a merchant and married Khadija, a wealthy widow. Mecca was a trading town and a place of pilgrimage, centred on the shrine of the Kaaba.

Around 610, Muslims believe, he began to receive revelations from God through the angel Gabriel, which were later gathered as the Quran. He preached that there is one God, that people will be judged, and that the rich must care for the poor. Mecca's leading families saw this as a threat to their gods and their trade, and persecuted his followers.

In 622 he and his followers moved to Medina, the Hijra, which marks year one of the Islamic calendar. In Medina he became the leader of a community bound by the Constitution of Medina.

  • After years of war with Mecca, he took the city in 630 with little bloodshed and cleared the idols from the Kaaba.
  • By his death in 632, most of Arabia was united under Islam.

He left no agreed successor. His friend Abu Bakr became the first caliph; a minority believed it should have been his cousin and son-in-law Ali, the root of the split between Sunni and Shia Islam. Within a century the caliphate reached from Spain to India.
sum: Muhammad was the Arab prophet and leader who founded Islam, born in Mecca in western Arabia around 570 and died in Medina in 632. Muslims believe he was the last prophet sent by God, after Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
